data.long_meaning: In Biblical times, Priscilla was an honorific title given to noble and respected women. In Acts 18:24, Priscilla and Aquila are mentioned as hosting Paul in their home and teaching him the ways of the Lord. The name Priscilla carries the meaning “Explaned, noble woman” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Priscilla usually hope their child will grow to embody explaned, noble woman and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of respect and honor for women in the early Christian community.
data.etymology: Priscilla belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Explaned, noble woman.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Priscilla total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_english.name: Priscilla
in_english.meaning: she who is freed, set free, liberated, freedwoman, noble
in_english.long_meaning: Priscilla is a feminine given name that originated from the Greek words 'prisca' and 'illa', meaning 'she who is freed' or 'set free'. In the New Testament, Priscilla is mentioned in the Epistle to the Colossians 4:3 and 2 Timothy 4:21 as a woman of the church in Colossae, who accompanied her husband Aquila and was a companion of Paul the Apostle. Priscilla is also mentioned in Acts 18:2, 18:18, 18:26 as a prominent woman in the early Christian church. The name Priscilla is associated with qualities of freedom, nobility, and leadership, making it a popular choice for Christian baby girls around the world.

data.cultural_impact: Priscilla was a woman of significant influence in the early Christian church. Her name, meaning 'ancient, venerable, or distinguished,' became synonymous with noble and respected women in Christianity. The name carries a sense of dignity and honor, symbolizing the power and influence of women in the Church and beyond.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Priscilla holds deep spiritual significance as it is mentioned in the Bible as the name of a woman of great faith and devotion. Priscilla and her husband, Aquila, played a crucial role in Paul's ministry and belonged to the group of early Christian leaders who spread the Good News throughout the ancient world. Their hospitality and teaching of Paul reflected the Christian values of generosity, wisdom, and dedication to the Word of God. Thus, the name Priscilla is a powerful reminder of the spiritual legacy left by the early Christian women who played essential roles in shaping the Christian faith.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Priscilla: Dedicated to God as a precious gem, bearing wisdom and strength in the service of Christ.

biblical_reference.note: Priscilla is mentioned in the New Testament as a woman of the church in Colossae and a companion of Paul the Apostle.

historical_references.reference: Priscilla and Aquila were early Christian missionaries from Rome who traveled throughout the Mediterranean world. They are mentioned in several New Testament letters, including Romans, 1 and 2 Corinthians, and Acts.
historical_references.context: Priscilla and Aquila are believed to have met and been married before their conversion to Christianity. They were tentmakers by trade and traveled with Paul on his missionary journeys. Priscilla is noted for teaching Apollos about the way of God more accurately (Acts 18:24-26).

historical_references.reference: Priscilla of Aquitaine (c. 640 – c. 673 AD) was a Frankish princess who became a Benedictine abbess. She is considered one of the pioneers of the Benedictine Reform, which aimed to restore the observance of the Rule of St. Benedict in the monasteries.
historical_references.context: Priscilla was the eldest daughter of Anselm, Duke of Austrasia and Austrasia, and his wife Balthilde. She was raised in the monastery of Chelles, where her mother was the abbess. Priscilla later became the abbess of the monastery of Faremoutiers. She is known for her leadership, her extensive correspondence, and her efforts to promote the study of Latin and Greek.

modern_usage.modern_context: Priscilla is a name of Latin origin that means 'ancestor, elder, venerable'. In modern times, the name Priscilla has been associated with women who are leaders in their fields, advocates for interfaith dialogue, and champions for education. On professional networking site LinkedIn, Priscillas are often found in leadership roles, breaking glass ceilings and setting new industry standards. On Instagram, Priscillas share their stories of empowerment and inspire others to do the same through self-love and body positivity movements. At TED Talks, Priscillas take the stage to share their innovative ideas and perspectives, contributing to global dialogue and pushing boundaries.
